brief: Verdict ahead of the print: revenue is not the test; ARR timing and funding are.
Kona: benchmark GPU financing and prepayment terms by tenant credit.
changes: Report date set: 5 November 2026, for the quarter to 30 September (fiscal 1Q FY27; recorded as 2026Q3 by calendar).
FY27 capex guided to $25bn to $30bn against about $14bn secured and about $8bn more targeted in GPU financing and prepayments.
Operating ARR about $1bn as of 26 August; over $4bn targeted by 31 December, mostly late in the quarter.
Stock down about 42% in a month to 2 November, amid a sector selloff after a Gartner survival forecast.
checks: Built before results. Date from company release via StockTitan and Manila Times; FY26 figures from the 27 August release; call items from the Investing.com transcript extract; consensus from Equibles (single source, marked in the card); prices from 24/7 Wall St. dated 2 November. Market cap at $22.96 derived in code from TopOne's $10.3bn at $25.43 (about 405mn shares), so approximate. No bond or CDS quote or adjusted EBITDA consensus found. Not independently rechecked by a subagent.
consensus_thesis: Investors own IREN as a former miner with owned power that is turning into a GPU cloud, with over $4bn of contracted ARR for 2026 capacity against a market cap near $9.3bn at $22.96 on 2 November (about 405mn shares implied by TopOne's $10.3bn at $25.43). The stock has fallen about 40% in a month in a sector selloff over debt-funded builds, so the market is paying for the contracts while doubting the funding. Positioning is contested: 15 of 20 ratings are Buy or better with a $77.81 average target, yet short interest was about 20.7% on 30 September. No bond or CDS quote was found; the last marks are the 6.0% Microsoft GPU financing and the 9.0% Mackenzie facility.
headline: Fiscal 1Q FY27 revenue (consensus about $221mn) matters less than whether $4bn of contracted ARR goes live by December and how IREN closes a $3bn to $8bn funding gap against $25bn to $30bn of FY27 capex, with the stock near $23 and about 21% of shares sold short.
kona: IREN shows how GPU financing prices by tenant: about 6% and 96% of capex with prepayments for Microsoft, against 9.0% and about 90% for non-investment-grade deployments. If Kona owns GPUs, expect the higher band or worse without an investment-grade contract. IREN's prepayments at 45% to 55% of GPU capex are the benchmark to ask of tenants.

name: IREN

questions.question: In August you guided $25bn to $30bn of capex against about $14bn secured and about $8bn targeted. How much of the target closed since 30 June, at what price, and what funds the remaining $3bn to $8bn? Will you rule out common equity below $30?
questions.why: With the stock near $23, the funding mix decides per-share value.

questions.question: Operating ARR was about $1bn in August against over $4bn by December. What is it today, on what date did Microsoft accept Horizon 2, and what share of December ARR bills for more than 30 days in the quarter?
questions.why: Consensus $392mn next quarter depends on this timing.

questions.question: The Microsoft financing cost about 6% and Mackenzie 9.0%. What rate would you pay today on a non-investment-grade contract, and what advance rate? What is the first data center financing's size and recourse?
questions.why: Tests whether contracts still earn above funding cost as credit widens.

questions.question: You price above $20mn per IT MW on 3-year terms. At six-year GPU depreciation, what residual do you assume at contract end, and what operating margin results? Give the margin on Horizon 1.
questions.why: EBITDA hides the depreciation that decides returns.

questions.question: Microsoft is near half of December ARR. How much of 2027 capacity is signed with others, and name the MW and tenant type by date.

risks: Late-December commissioning pushes revenue into March.
Funding gap met with equity at depressed prices.
Rising GPU financing costs for non-investment-grade tenants.
Mining wind-down and Texas large-load policy.

sections.body: IREN owns powered sites (Childress, Sweetwater, Mackenzie and others) and the GPUs on them, and sells AI cloud on 3-year to 5-year contracts with large prepayments. Revenue = active IT MW x price per MW-year (recent 3-year contracts above $20mn per IT MW; talks near $25mn, per FY26 release). Mining is being decommissioned by end December 2026.

sections.body: Equibles forecasts $239.9mn for 1Q against $221.3mn consensus. FY27 EPS: Equibles shows a loss of $3.42, while Zacks (1 September) expected a profit, likely stale. Debt-to-equity 1.87 appears in press only.

sections.body: At 30 June: cash $5,895.6mn plus restricted $1,724.0mn; debt about $7.59bn excluding finance leases. $3.6bn Microsoft GPU financing at about 6%; $2.4bn Mackenzie facility at 9.0% fixed (Blue Owl, PIMCO funds); $2.8bn new GPU financings in total. About $19bn raised in 12 months, including about $3bn of equity (FY26 call).
